page.layout: One column of verse, centred on the page, with the stanza lines indented in the printed pattern. At the lower right below the last line, the catchword "Quod". No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Captusq;[?] grandi munere mittitur Augusta sacra limina qui domus Perrupit audax,& retecto Ense tuum latus appetiuit. Hac arte Princeps concidit Auricus, Quo dura fortes vindice vincula Rupere Belgæ,quum Tyrannus Iussit Iber violare leges, Iurata Genti fœdera subruens. Hæc Roma monstrat perfida,quæ fidem Pactámque dextram Christianis Fraude noua temerare sancit[?]. Cur pace facta,Tygride fœuior, Heu Roma quæris sub iuga mittere Hispana bellaces Britannos, Innocuumque caput fatigas? Urit profanos fœmina Præsules Dilecta Calo,cui placet obsequi Christo docenti: cuique cordi est Ardua cum pietate Virtus. Urit cruentis quod cruciatibus Dulcem coactos linquere Patriam Solatur,& Christum sequutos Hospitiis recreat benignis, Quod fida sacros auxiliis greges Firmat piorum non trepidantibus. Longofque Belgarum labores Marte potens miserata sanat.

page.notes: Printed "Captusq" carries a superscript mark that is not fully clear; the q; reading is doubtful. "sancit" is read from a long-s form and is doubtful. "retecto" is a faint reading. The "A" of "Augusta" is a decorated initial, joined to the word. The catchword "Quod" stands alone at the lower right and is not repeated in the text.
